title: All Five 'Letters' of DNA Found in an Ancient Asteroid
summary: All five of the molecular "letters" of DNA and RNA have been found in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid. A new study reports that all five fundamental nucleobases have been detected in samples from the asteroid Ryugu, which Japan's Hayabusa2 mission brought back to Earth in 2020. The study, published in the journal Nature Astronomy, was carried out by a team of Japanese scientists. Nucleobases are nitrogen-containing organic molecules that spell out genetic information in DNA and RNA. The five main ones are adenine and guanine, known as purines, and cytosine, thymine and uracil, known as pyrimidines. They combine with sugars and phosphates to make nucleotides, the building blocks of genetic material. Without them, the genetic code that lets organisms grow, reproduce and evolve would not exist. This is not the first time scientists have spotted these molecules in space rock. In 2023, an international team reported finding uracil, one of the five, in the same Ryugu samples. Meteorites that fell to Earth have also yielded nucleobases, and samples from NASA's mission to the asteroid Bennu yielded all five in 2025. But meteorites that land on Earth can be contaminated along the way. The Ryugu samples are different: Hayabusa2 delivered 5.4 grams of pristine material, collected in space and protected from Earth's contamination, so researchers could study it in ultra-clean labs. They extracted the organic molecules using water and hydrochloric acid, then purified them for testing, and found all five nucleobases in both samples they analysed, in roughly similar amounts. The results suggest that the ingredients for life may have been widespread throughout the early Solar System. Asteroids like Ryugu are leftovers from the Solar System's early days. Together, the findings suggest that key parts of genetic material may have formed in space and later been delivered to the early Earth.
why_it_matters: If the building blocks of life came from space, the story of life on Earth is part of a much bigger cosmic story.
